newsitem.title: ITALY: BOF's Albert says EMU delay would push up rates.
newsitem.headline: BOF's Albert says EMU delay would push up rates.

text.p: Michel Albert, member of the Bank of France monetary policy council, said on Monday that a delay in the introduction of Europe's single currency would push up interest rates, especially in Italy, France and Spain.

Albert, speaking in French at a convention in Rome on globalisation of markets, said delay in European monetary and economic union (EMU) would "lead to an overvaluation of the strongest currencies with downwards pressure on those that are weaker".
"There would therefore be a rise in interest rates...this would hit Italy, France and Spain in particular," he said.
Albert said financial markets had shown confidence that EMU, set for launch on January 1, 1999 among countries which meet the criteria, would be achieved.
"That has allowed rates to fall. If there were to be a delay in monetary union the problems of financing public debt would be worrying," he said.
"If the (launch) date is respected, we will all derive benefit," Albert added.
